events.affected_or_evacuated: About 700,000 displaced (Red Cross / commonly cited figure)
events.notes: 246 is the American Red Cross figure commonly cited by NOAA. Levee breaches were part of a wider river flood, not a single dam failure.
events.name: Great Mississippi Flood of 1927
events.geo_source: Greenville, a principal city on the flooded lower Mississippi
events.what_happened: The most destructive river flood in US history to that date. After months of rain, the Mississippi broke levees from Illinois to Louisiana in 1927, inundating about 27,000 square miles. The American Red Cross recorded 246 deaths; some later estimates are higher. Hundreds of thousands were displaced. The disaster led to the 1928 Flood Control Act.
events.status: Historical. Federal flood-control system rebuilt after 1928.
events.cause_summary: Months of heavy rain over the Mississippi basin; widespread levee breaches on the lower river.

sources.label: NOAA: The Great Mississippi River Flood of 1927

events.name: 1931 China floods
events.geo_source: Wuhan, core inundated city on the Yangtze
events.what_happened: From June to August 1931 the Yangtze, Huai, Yellow River and Grand Canal flooded after prolonged rains, inundating a core zone across eight central provinces and hitting Wuhan and Nanjing. On 25 August dikes near Gaoyou Lake failed; in Gaoyou County alone 18,000 people drowned. Fatality estimates vary widely, from Li Wenhai’s 422,420 (media-based) to official figures around 2 million including famine and disease, and some Western claims of 3.7–4 million.
events.status: Historical. Among the deadliest floods on record.
events.affected_or_evacuated: Government estimate 25 million affected; later historians up to 53 million. Inundation about 181,500 km².
events.cause_summary: Prolonged summer rains over the Yangtze–Huai basin, culminating in dike failure at Gaoyou Lake.
events.notes: Deaths left unknown on the pin because sourced estimates span 422,420 to about 4 million (drowning vs famine/disease). Do not treat as zero.

events.name: North Sea flood of 1953
events.geo_source: Oude-Tonge, one of the highest local death tolls (305)
events.what_happened: A severe European windstorm plus a high spring tide drove a North Sea storm surge on the night of 31 January–1 February 1953. Dutch sea defences failed in many places (67 breaches in Zeeland alone). Wikipedia records 2,551 fatalities overall: 1,836 in the Netherlands, 307 on land in England, 19 in eastern Scotland, 28 in Belgium, and more than 230 at sea including the sinking of MV Princess Victoria. Led to the Delta Works and the Thames Barrier.
events.status: Historical. Defences rebuilt (Delta Works, Thames Barrier).
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 70,000 emergency evacuations in the Netherlands; 30,000+ people forced from homes in the UK.
events.cause_summary: North Sea windstorm coincident with a high spring tide; sea defences overtopped and breached.
events.notes: 2,551 is the Wikipedia infobox total (land plus sea). Dutch land deaths 1,836; UK land 307.
events.inundation_area: 1,365 km² of Dutch land flooded (9% of farmland)
events.economic_damage: About 1 billion Dutch guilders; UK about £50 million (1953)

events.name: Great Flood of 1993
events.geo_source: St. Louis, a principal city on the flooded middle Mississippi
events.what_happened: Persistent heavy rain from spring into summer 1993 produced a months-long flood on the upper Mississippi and Missouri. NOAA and NWS treat it as one of the most damaging river floods in US history. About 50 people died. Some 54,000 people were evacuated. Damage about $15 billion (1993 USD). Hundreds of levees were overtopped or breached as part of the wider river flood.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 54,000 evacuated (NOAA/NWS summaries)
events.cause_summary: Months of above-normal rainfall over the upper Midwest, saturating the Mississippi–Missouri system.

sources.label: NWS Davenport: The Great Flood of 1993

events.notes: 50 deaths and ~$15 billion are the NOAA/NWS figures. Levee breaches were part of a wider river flood.

events.name: 1998 China floods
events.geo_source: Wuhan, principal city on the flooded middle Yangtze
events.what_happened: Summer 1998 monsoon rains produced severe flooding along the Yangtze and other Chinese rivers. Official Chinese figures recorded 4,150 deaths, 18 million people made homeless, and about 180 million people affected.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 180 million affected; 18 million homeless (official figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.cause_summary: Prolonged monsoon rainfall over the Yangtze basin.
events.notes: 4,150 is the official nationwide figure commonly cited (not Yangtze-only).

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 2.7 million affected in Honduras; millions more regionally
events.rainfall_mm: Locally more than 900 mm; some Honduran stations over 1,000 mm
events.notes: 11,374 is the Wikipedia infobox total. NHC contemporaneous estimates were around 9,000–11,000.
events.name: Hurricane Mitch floods
events.geo_source: Tegucigalpa, capital heavily damaged by flooding and landslides
events.what_happened: Hurricane Mitch stalled over Central America in late October 1998. Extreme rainfall produced catastrophic floods and landslides, especially in Honduras and Nicaragua. Wikipedia records about 11,374 deaths. Most deaths were from freshwater flooding, not wind.
events.cause_summary: Stalling tropical cyclone with extreme multi-day rainfall over mountainous Central America.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Tens of thousands displaced; about 8,000 homes destroyed (commonly cited)
events.rainfall_mm: Maiquetía about 911 mm in 52 hours (commonly cited)
events.notes: Deaths left unknown because sourced estimates span about 10,000–30,000. Do not treat as zero.
events.name: 1999 Vargas tragedy
events.geo_source: Caraballeda alluvial fan, among the worst-hit coastal towns
events.what_happened: Days of extreme rainfall on the coastal range above Vargas State in mid-December 1999 produced debris flows and flash floods that buried towns on the Caribbean fans. Death-toll estimates range from about 10,000 to 30,000; no single official figure is settled. It is the deadliest Venezuelan natural disaster on record.
events.cause_summary: Extreme multi-day rainfall on steep coastal catchments, producing debris flows onto alluvial fans.

events.affected_or_evacuated: More than 1 million affected; about 250,000 displaced
events.notes: About 800 deaths is the commonly cited Wikipedia/ReliefWeb figure.
events.name: 2000 Mozambique floods
events.geo_source: Chókwè on the Limpopo, a principal flooded town
events.what_happened: Cyclones Connie and Eline and weeks of rain in February–March 2000 produced Mozambique’s worst flood in living memory. Wikipedia records about 800 deaths and more than 1 million people affected.
events.cause_summary: Sequential tropical cyclones and extreme rainfall over southern Mozambique river basins.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Tens of thousands stranded in Mumbai; statewide displacement in the lakhs
events.rainfall_mm: Santacruz 944 mm in 24 hours on 26 July 2005
events.notes: 1,094 is the Maharashtra total commonly cited; 447 of those in Mumbai.
events.name: 2005 Maharashtra floods
events.geo_source: Mumbai city; Santacruz recorded 944 mm in 24 hours
events.what_happened: On 26 July 2005, Mumbai recorded 944 mm of rain in 24 hours at Santacruz. The city and much of Maharashtra flooded. Wikipedia records 1,094 deaths in Maharashtra (including 447 in Mumbai).
events.cause_summary: Record 24-hour monsoon rainfall over Mumbai plus overwhelmed urban drainage.

events.name: Hurricane Katrina flooding
events.river_or_facility: Lake Pontchartrain and New Orleans levee system
events.geo_source: New Orleans city center; 80% of the city flooded after 53 levee breaches
events.what_happened: Katrina made landfall near Buras-Triumph, Louisiana, on 29 August 2005 as a Category 3 hurricane. Storm surge caused 53 breaches in the federally built New Orleans hurricane-protection system; about 80% of the city flooded. NHC updated the fatality count on 4 January 2023 to 1,392 (down from the older 1,833 estimate). Damage about $125 billion (2005 USD). The largest loss of life was from the flooding, not wind.
events.status: Historical. Levee system rebuilt. Name Katrina retired.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 1.2 million under evacuation orders; over 1 million displaced; 26,000 sheltered in the Superdome.
events.cause_summary: Hurricane storm surge plus engineering failures in the New Orleans levee and floodwall system.
events.notes: Dam/levee structural failures are also in the dam database where we have a New Orleans/Katrina levee record; this is the wider flood event. Deaths are the NHC 2023 figure (1,392), not the older 1,833.
events.inundation_area: 80% of New Orleans; federal declarations covered 90,000 sq mi

events.name: 2010 Pakistan floods
events.geo_source: Nowshera on the Kabul/Indus system; KP had most deaths
events.what_happened: Heavy monsoon rains from late July 2010 flooded the Indus basin. About one-fifth of Pakistan’s land area was affected. Wikipedia records 1,985 deaths nationwide, with more than 90% of deaths in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Pakistani government data: about 20 million people directly affected. UN described it as among the worst disasters of that period. Estimated economic impact up to about $43 billion.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 20 million directly affected
events.cause_summary: Exceptional monsoon rainfall over northern Pakistan, flooding the Indus and destroying infrastructure already weakened in KP.
events.notes: Injured 2,966 from mid-September government tally cited on Wikipedia. Earlier FFC mid-August tally was lower.
events.rainfall_mm: Peshawar 333 mm in the late-July wet spell; Risalpur 415 mm
events.inundation_area: About one-fifth of Pakistan’s land area
events.economic_damage: Up to about $43 billion (estimate cited on Wikipedia)

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 200,000 affected
events.economic_damage: About A$2.38 billion insured (ICA figure commonly cited)
events.notes: 35 deaths is the commonly cited official/Wikipedia figure. Wivenhoe Dam operations were examined; this is not recorded as a dam failure.
events.name: 2010–11 Queensland floods
events.geo_source: Brisbane CBD, inundated in January 2011
events.what_happened: A prolonged La Niña wet season produced flooding across much of Queensland from December 2010 into January 2011. Toowoomba and the Lockyer Valley were hit by a 10 January flash flood; Brisbane and Ipswich flooded days later. Wikipedia records 35 deaths. About 200,000 people were affected.
events.cause_summary: Prolonged La Niña rainfall, then extreme falls over the Toowoomba escarpment and Brisbane catchment.

events.name: 2011 Thailand floods
events.geo_source: Ayutthaya, heavily inundated industrial and historic city north of Bangkok
events.what_happened: The 2011 monsoon flooded much of central Thailand, including Ayutthaya and parts of the Bangkok metropolitan area, for months. Thai official figures recorded 815 deaths. About 13.6 million people were affected. World Bank damage estimate about US$45–46 billion.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 13.6 million affected
events.cause_summary: Exceptional monsoon rainfall over the Chao Phraya basin, prolonged inundation of the central plain.
events.notes: 815 is the Thai official death toll commonly cited.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Hundreds of thousands evacuated; 8.5 million without power
events.notes: 233 is the NHC/Wikipedia combined death toll. US deaths 157.
events.name: Hurricane Sandy coastal flooding
events.location_label: Lower Manhattan / New York Harbor, USA
events.geo_source: Battery Park / lower Manhattan, inundated by storm surge
events.river_or_basin: New York Harbor / Hudson / Atlantic coast
events.what_happened: Hurricane Sandy made landfall near Brigantine, New Jersey, on 29 October 2012. A record storm surge flooded New York Harbor, lower Manhattan, Staten Island and the New Jersey shore. NHC recorded 233 deaths in the United States, Caribbean and Bahamas combined (157 in the US). Damage about $70 billion (2012 USD).
events.cause_summary: Post-tropical cyclone storm surge into New York Harbor and the New Jersey coast.
events.river_or_facility: New York Harbor / Hudson / Atlantic coast

events.name: 2013 European floods
events.geo_source: Passau at the Inn–Danube confluence, a record-stage city in 2013
events.what_happened: Late May–June 2013 flooding on the Elbe and Danube after extreme rain in Central Europe. Wikipedia records 25 deaths. Several countries issued disaster declarations. Passau recorded a record Danube stage.
events.affected_or_evacuated: Tens of thousands evacuated in Germany, Austria, Czechia and Hungary
events.cause_summary: Extreme late-spring rainfall over the Elbe and Danube catchments.
events.notes: 25 deaths is the Wikipedia infobox total.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 110,000 people evacuated from the pilgrimage zone (commonly cited)
events.notes: Deaths left unknown because official confirmed-dead vs missing figures are reported differently (hundreds confirmed; combined dead/missing commonly about 5,700). Do not treat as zero.
events.name: 2013 Uttarakhand floods
events.geo_source: Kedarnath temple town, buried by debris flows on 16–17 June 2013
events.what_happened: A mid-June 2013 cloudburst and extreme rain over the Kedarnath–Mandakini catchment produced debris flows and flash floods that destroyed the pilgrimage town and downstream valleys. Official figures recorded thousands dead or missing (commonly cited combined toll around 5,700). Not a dam failure.
events.cause_summary: Extreme orographic rainfall and cloudburst over the Mandakini headwaters, producing debris flows.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 100,000 evacuated in Alberta
events.notes: Included for the scale of evacuation and official disaster declarations, not the death toll alone.
events.name: 2013 Alberta floods
events.geo_source: Calgary downtown at the Bow–Elbow confluence
events.what_happened: Extreme June 2013 rain on the eastern slopes of the Rockies flooded the Bow, Elbow and Highwood. Calgary’s downtown and many riverside communities were evacuated. Wikipedia records 5 deaths. About 100,000 people were evacuated in Alberta — the largest evacuation in the province’s history.
events.cause_summary: Extreme rainfall on the eastern slopes, flooding the Bow–Elbow system through Calgary.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 1.6 million affected; hundreds of thousands evacuated
events.notes: 86 is the Wikipedia infobox total.
events.name: 2014 Southeast Europe floods
events.geo_source: Doboj, one of the worst-hit Bosnian towns
events.what_happened: A slow-moving cyclone in mid-May 2014 produced the worst flooding in the western Balkans in more than a century. Wikipedia records 86 deaths. Towns including Doboj, Obrenovac and Šamac were inundated. Serbia and Bosnia declared emergencies.
events.cause_summary: Slow-moving cyclone with extreme rainfall over the Sava basin.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Hundreds of thousands displaced; Srinagar city evacuated in large part
events.notes: 557 is the Wikipedia combined total (India 280, Pakistan 277).
events.name: 2014 India–Pakistan floods
events.region: Jammu and Kashmir / Pakistani Punjab / Azad Kashmir
events.geo_source: Srinagar city, inundated in September 2014
events.what_happened: Early September 2014 monsoon rains flooded the Kashmir Valley and parts of Pakistani Punjab. Srinagar was inundated. Wikipedia records 557 deaths (280 in Indian-administered Kashmir and adjoining states; 277 in Pakistan).
events.cause_summary: Extreme late-monsoon rainfall over the Jhelum catchment.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 1.8 million displaced (commonly cited)
events.rainfall_mm: Chennai about 1,200 mm in November 2015 (city record month)
events.notes: 500 is the Wikipedia infobox total. Dam_release is a contributing operational factor, not a dam-break.
events.name: 2015 South Indian floods
events.geo_source: Chennai city, inundated in November–December 2015
events.what_happened: A strong northeast monsoon in November–December 2015 flooded Chennai and coastal Tamil Nadu. Wikipedia records 500 deaths. Chembarambakkam and other reservoirs released water as levels rose — a contributing operational factor, not a dam failure.
events.cause_summary: Extreme northeast-monsoon rainfall over Chennai; urban drainage overwhelmed; reservoir releases as a contributing factor.

events.name: Hurricane Harvey flooding
events.geo_source: Houston city center; stalling tropical cyclone produced multi-day urban/river flooding
events.what_happened: Harvey stalled over southeast Texas after landfall on 25 August 2017 and dropped extreme multi-day rain on the Houston metropolitan area. NHC recorded 68 direct deaths in the United States (103 total US deaths including indirect). Damage about $125 billion. Cedar Bayou recorded 60.58 inches of rain.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 39,000 people in Texas shelters at peak; more than 300,000 structures flooded
events.cause_summary: Stalling tropical cyclone with extreme rainfall over the Houston metro area.
events.notes: 68 is the NHC direct US death toll. NHC total US deaths including indirect: 103. Wikipedia infobox often lists 107.
events.rainfall_mm: Cedar Bayou 60.58 inches (1,539 mm), US tropical-cyclone rainfall record

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 8 million under evacuation orders at peak
events.notes: 225 is the Wikipedia infobox death toll.
events.name: 2018 Japan floods
events.geo_source: Mabi district of Kurashiki, among the worst-hit communities
events.what_happened: A stationary front and Typhoon Prapiroon remnant moisture produced extreme rain over western Japan in early July 2018. Wikipedia records 225 deaths, mostly in Hiroshima, Okayama and Ehime. Mabi (Kurashiki) was inundated after river overflows.
events.cause_summary: Stationary seasonal front with extreme rainfall over western Honshu and Shikoku.

events.name: 2018 Kerala floods
events.geo_source: Kochi, principal city in the flooded coastal plain
events.what_happened: Extreme monsoon rain in August 2018 produced Kerala’s worst flood in decades. Wikipedia records 483 deaths and about 1.4 million people evacuated to relief camps. Several reservoirs released water as levels rose — a contributing operational factor, not a dam failure.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 1.4 million evacuated to relief camps; 5.4 million affected (state figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.cause_summary: Extreme monsoon rainfall; some reservoirs released water as levels rose (sourced as a contributing operational factor, not a dam failure).
events.notes: 483 is the Kerala government / Wikipedia figure. Not a dam-break record.

events.name: Cyclone Idai floods
events.region: Sofala / Beira / Zambezi / eastern Zimbabwe / Malawi
events.geo_source: Beira, landfall city and the worst-hit urban area
events.what_happened: Tropical Cyclone Idai made landfall near Beira on 14 March 2019 and produced catastrophic flooding in central Mozambique, eastern Zimbabwe and Malawi. Wikipedia records more than 1,300 deaths (Mozambique 603, Zimbabwe 344, Malawi 60, plus later updates). Beira was largely destroyed.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 3 million affected across Mozambique, Zimbabwe and Malawi (OCHA figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.cause_summary: Landfalling tropical cyclone with extreme rainfall and storm surge over a low-lying coastal plain.
events.notes: 1,300 is a conservative rounded combined figure. Country subtotals 603+344+60 already exceed 1,000; later tallies go higher.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 63 million affected (official figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.economic_damage: About 178 billion yuan direct economic loss (official figure cited on Wikipedia)
events.notes: 219 is the Wikipedia official death toll. Not a dam-break event.
events.name: 2020 China floods
events.geo_source: Poyang Lake / Jiujiang, a core 2020 inundation zone
events.what_happened: The 2020 mei-yu / monsoon season produced severe flooding along the Yangtze and Huai. Wikipedia records 219 deaths and about 63 million people affected. The Three Gorges Reservoir was operated for flood-control storage; this record is the wider river flood, not a dam failure.
events.cause_summary: Prolonged mei-yu rainfall over the Yangtze and Huai basins.

events.name: 2021 European floods
events.geo_source: Altenahr in the Ahr valley, among the worst-hit communes
events.what_happened: A stalled storm complex (low Bernd) dropped extreme rain over western Germany, eastern Belgium and neighbouring countries on 12–15 July 2021. Rivers including the Ahr and Vesdre rose in hours. Wikipedia: at least 243 deaths (196 Germany, 39 Belgium, 2 Romania, 1 Italy, 1 Austria). Jalhay, Belgium, recorded 271.5 mm in 48 hours. Insured losses at least €2 billion; total damage around €46 billion / $54 billion. Deadliest German natural disaster since the 1962 North Sea flood.
events.status: Historical. Rebuilding in the Ahr valley continued for years.
events.affected_or_evacuated: Tens of thousands evacuated in Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands (Venlo 10,000+).
events.cause_summary: Slow-moving summer low with record 24–48 hour rainfall over steep mid-mountain catchments.
events.notes: Germany deaths later reported as 196 including 135 in Rhineland-Palatinate (Ahrweiler) and 47 in NRW. Infobox total 243.
events.rainfall_mm: Jalhay 271.5 mm / 48 h; Reifferscheid 207 mm / 9 h
events.economic_damage: About $54 billion (2021 USD); Germany direct damage ~€33.4 billion

events.name: 2021 Henan floods
events.river_or_facility: Yellow River tributaries / Zhengzhou urban drainage
events.geo_source: Zhengzhou, including the metro flooding
events.what_happened: Extreme July 2021 rainfall over Henan, especially Zhengzhou, flooded the city and surrounding counties, including a well-documented metro disaster. Official provincial figures recorded 398 deaths. Zhengzhou saw 201.9 mm in one hour.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 14.5 million affected in Henan (official figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.cause_summary: Extreme hourly rainfall over Zhengzhou and the surrounding Henan plain.
events.notes: 398 is the official Henan death toll after investigation. This is the wider flood, not a levee-only pin.
events.rainfall_mm: Zhengzhou 201.9 mm in one hour; 624 mm in a day

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 17,000 evacuated
events.notes: Included for evacuations and official emergency declarations. Dike failures were part of the wider flood.
events.name: 2021 British Columbia floods
events.location_label: Abbotsford / Sumas Prairie, British Columbia, Canada
events.geo_source: Abbotsford / Sumas Prairie, a principal inundated farming district
events.what_happened: An atmospheric river in mid-November 2021 washed out highways and flooded the Fraser Valley, Merritt and Princeton. Wikipedia records 5 deaths. About 17,000 people were evacuated. Sumas Prairie was inundated after dike failures as part of a wider atmospheric-river flood.
events.cause_summary: Atmospheric-river rainfall on already-burned and saturated catchments; dike failures as part of a wider flood.

events.name: 2022 eastern Australia floods
events.geo_source: Lismore CBD, record Wilsons River flood
events.what_happened: A series of extreme rain events in February–March 2022 flooded southeast Queensland and the NSW Northern Rivers. Lismore recorded a record Wilsons River flood. Wikipedia records 22 deaths.
events.affected_or_evacuated: Tens of thousands evacuated; Lismore CBD largely destroyed
events.cause_summary: Repeated extreme rainfall events over already-saturated catchments in SEQ and the NSW Northern Rivers.
events.notes: 22 deaths is the Wikipedia infobox figure.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 40,000 displaced (government figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.notes: 448 is the Wikipedia infobox death toll.
events.name: 2022 KwaZulu-Natal floods
events.geo_source: Durban / eThekwini, the principal urban disaster zone
events.what_happened: Extreme mid-April 2022 rainfall over KwaZulu-Natal produced deadly flash floods and landslides around Durban. Wikipedia records 448 deaths. President Ramaphosa declared a national state of disaster. It is South Africa’s deadliest weather disaster on record.
events.cause_summary: Extreme coastal rainfall over informal settlements and steep urban catchments around Durban.

events.name: 2022 Pakistan floods
events.geo_source: Shahdadkot, Sindh, widely photographed under floodwater
events.what_happened: From mid-June through October 2022, heavier-than-usual monsoon rain and glacial melt flooded large parts of Pakistan. Wikipedia: 1,739–1,760 deaths, 12,867 injured, about 33 million people affected, 2.1 million left homeless. Sindh recorded 799 deaths. The government declared a state of emergency on 25 August. Damage estimates include $14.9–15.2 billion (Ministry of Finance / UNDP) and about $40 billion (World Bank / Pakistan Climate Change Council). UNOSAT mapped about 75,000 km² flooded (around 9–12% of the country), not the “one-third underwater” claim.
events.status: Historical. Recovery and climate-resilient reconstruction ongoing.
events.affected_or_evacuated: 33 million affected; 2.1 million homeless; 8 million displaced (figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.cause_summary: Extreme monsoon rainfall (Sindh ~784% of August average) plus glacial melt after a severe heat wave.
events.notes: Infobox lists 1,760 deaths; lead says 1,739. Pin uses 1,739. Do not use the “one-third of the country underwater” line as a measured inundation figure.
events.inundation_area: UNOSAT ~75,000 km²; USAID peak standing water ~32,800 sq mi
events.economic_damage: About $40 billion (World Bank / PCCC); MoF damage ~$14.9 billion

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 1.4 million displaced; 3.2 million affected (NEMA figures cited on Wikipedia)
events.notes: 603 is the NEMA/Wikipedia death toll. Dam_release refers to transboundary Lagdo operations, not a Nigerian dam break.
events.name: 2022 Nigeria floods
events.geo_source: Lokoja at the Niger–Benue confluence, a principal flooded city
events.what_happened: The 2022 wet season produced Nigeria’s worst flood in a decade. NEMA / Wikipedia record 603 deaths, about 2,400 injured and 1.4 million displaced. Cameroon’s Lagdo Dam releases were discussed as a contributing factor — this record is the wider river flood, not a Nigerian dam failure.
events.cause_summary: Extreme wet-season rainfall on the Niger–Benue; Lagdo Dam releases cited as a contributing transboundary factor.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Thousands evacuated; 10,000+ households displaced in Hawke's Bay (commonly cited)
events.notes: 11 deaths is the Wikipedia infobox figure.
events.name: Cyclone Gabrielle floods
events.location_label: Esk Valley / Napier, Hawke's Bay, New Zealand
events.geo_source: Esk Valley north of Napier, among the worst-hit communities
events.what_happened: Cyclone Gabrielle struck the North Island in February 2023. Extreme rain produced catastrophic flooding and debris flows in Hawke's Bay and Tairāwhiti. Wikipedia records 11 deaths. A national state of emergency was declared.
events.cause_summary: Ex-tropical cyclone with extreme rainfall over Hawke's Bay and Tairāwhiti.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 50,000 evacuated
events.economic_damage: About €8.5–10 billion (Italian government estimates cited on Wikipedia)
events.notes: 17 deaths is the Wikipedia infobox figure.
events.name: 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods
events.geo_source: Faenza, one of the worst-hit towns in May 2023
events.what_happened: Two extreme rain events in May 2023 flooded Emilia-Romagna. Wikipedia records 17 deaths. Twenty-three rivers burst their banks. About 50,000 people were evacuated. Italy declared a state of emergency.
events.cause_summary: Two extreme May rainfall events on already-saturated Emilia-Romagna catchments.

events.name: 2024 Kenya floods
events.geo_source: Mai Mahiu, site of a deadly washout widely reported in April 2024
events.what_happened: Heavy March–May 2024 long rains produced deadly floods and landslides across Kenya, including a well-reported disaster at Mai Mahiu. Kenya Red Cross / Wikipedia figures for Kenya are around 228 deaths as part of the wider East Africa floods.
events.affected_or_evacuated: Hundreds of thousands displaced across Kenya and neighbouring countries
events.cause_summary: Extreme long-rains rainfall and flash flooding, including a railway embankment washout at Mai Mahiu.
events.notes: 228 is a Kenya-focused figure cited on the 2024 East Africa floods page. Wider regional totals are higher.

events.name: 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods
events.location_label: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
events.geo_source: Porto Alegre waterfront on Lake Guaíba
events.what_happened: Extreme April–May 2024 rainfall produced the worst flood in Rio Grande do Sul in decades, inundating Porto Alegre and the Taquari and Jacuí valleys. Civil defence / Wikipedia record 183 deaths and about 581,000 people displaced.
events.affected_or_evacuated: About 581,000 displaced; 2.3 million affected (civil defence / Wikipedia)
events.cause_summary: Prolonged extreme rainfall over the Guaíba–Taquari basin.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods

events.notes: 183 is the Wikipedia/civil-defence death toll.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Hundreds of thousands evacuated in northern Vietnam
events.notes: 345 is the Vietnam-focused death toll commonly cited on the Typhoon Yagi page. Regional totals including Myanmar are higher.
events.name: Typhoon Yagi floods
events.region: Northern Vietnam / Red River Delta / Myanmar / Laos
events.geo_source: Hải Phòng, a principal landfall/flood city in northern Vietnam
events.what_happened: Typhoon Yagi, the strongest storm to hit the South China Sea in decades, made landfall in northern Vietnam in September 2024. Extreme rain produced widespread flooding and landslides. Wikipedia records hundreds of deaths in Vietnam (commonly cited around 345 in Vietnam, with additional deaths in Myanmar and elsewhere).
events.cause_summary: Landfalling super typhoon with extreme rainfall over northern Vietnam.

events.name: 2024 Central European floods (Storm Boris)
events.region: Poland / Czechia / Austria / Hungary / Slovakia / Romania
events.geo_source: Kłodzko, one of the worst-hit Polish towns under Storm Boris
events.what_happened: Storm Boris in September 2024 produced severe flooding across Central Europe, especially Poland, Czechia and Austria. Wikipedia records 27 deaths. Kłodzko and other Sudeten towns were inundated. Several countries issued disaster declarations.
events.affected_or_evacuated: Tens of thousands evacuated in Poland, Czechia and Austria
events.cause_summary: Slow-moving Storm Boris with extreme rainfall over Central European river basins.
events.notes: 27 is the Wikipedia infobox total.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Hundreds of thousands without power; large-scale evacuations in Florida and the Carolinas
events.economic_damage: About $78 billion (NOAA NCEI billion-dollar disasters figure commonly cited)
events.notes: 250 is the Wikipedia/commonly cited US death toll. Most fatalities were inland flood deaths in North Carolina and neighbouring states.
events.name: Hurricane Helene flooding
events.geo_source: Asheville, a principal city in the western North Carolina flood disaster
events.what_happened: Hurricane Helene made landfall in Florida’s Big Bend on 26 September 2024, then dumped extreme rain on the southern Appalachians. Western North Carolina, including Asheville and the Swannanoa valley, saw catastrophic freshwater flooding. Wikipedia / NHC record about 250 deaths, making Helene the deadliest US mainland hurricane since Katrina. Most deaths were from inland flooding, not the coastal surge.
events.cause_summary: Landfalling hurricane plus extreme orographic rainfall over the southern Appalachians.

events.affected_or_evacuated: About 13,300 people required rescue; 1,200 houses destroyed or damaged (government / AP 1 Oct 2024)
events.notes: 224 is the 1 October 2024 government figure reported by AP and cited on Wikipedia. Infobox later lists 300+. Pin uses the dated official 224.
events.name: 2024 Nepal floods
events.geo_source: Kathmandu Valley, among the worst-hit areas in September 2024
events.what_happened: Late-September 2024 monsoon rain — Kathmandu’s heaviest since at least 1970 — flooded the Bagmati and Nakkhu and triggered landslides on highways out of the capital. The Government of Nepal / AP reported at least 224 deaths and 28 missing as of 1 October 2024. Wikipedia infobox later lists 300+.
events.cause_summary: Extreme late-monsoon rainfall over central Nepal, including the Kathmandu Valley.

events.name: 2024 Spain floods (DANA)
events.geo_source: Paiporta, ground-zero town (62 deaths reported there)
events.what_happened: On 29 October 2024 a DANA (isolated high-level low) dropped more than a year’s rain on parts of eastern Spain. Flash floods killed about 238 people, mostly in Valencia province. Turís recorded 184.6 mm in one hour (Spanish record). The 1973 New Turia canal spared Valencia city proper; towns to the south including Paiporta were inundated. Regional ES-alert SMS went out at 20:11, after the Poyo had already burst its banks. Munich Re: about €10.7 billion total damage. Spanish government data update 4 January 2025.
events.status: Recovery. Carlos Mazón resigned as regional president in November 2025 after criticism of the response.
events.affected_or_evacuated: 36,605 people rescued nationwide; 116,000+ insurance claims
events.cause_summary: Mediterranean DANA / cold drop with extreme hourly rainfall over the Poyo and Magro catchments.
events.notes: Infobox deaths 238. A citizenship table on the same page sums to 231; pin uses the infobox 238 from the government update cited there.
events.rainfall_mm: Chiva nearly 500 mm in a day; Turís 184.6 mm in one hour
events.economic_damage: ~€10.7 billion total; ~€3.5 billion insured (Wikipedia / Munich Re)

events.affected_or_evacuated: Over 1 million affected in earlier tallies; later figures several million in Punjab (NDMA / Wikipedia)
events.notes: 1,037+ is the Wikipedia infobox death toll as of the 2025 season write-up. Later sitreps may differ.
events.name: 2025 Pakistan monsoon floods
events.geo_source: Lahore / Punjab, a core 2025 monsoon flood zone
events.what_happened: The 2025 monsoon produced deadly floods across Pakistan from June into September, especially in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (including Buner and Swat) and Punjab. Wikipedia records 1,037+ deaths and 1,067+ injured. NDMA, provincial governments and the armed forces ran large rescue operations.
events.cause_summary: Extreme 2025 monsoon rainfall over the Indus basin.

events.affected_or_evacuated: Hundreds rescued; federal disaster declaration for Kerr County and later others
events.rainfall_mm: 20.33 inches (516 mm) northwest of Streeter near Mason
events.notes: 136 is the Wikipedia county table total (Kerr 117, Travis 10, Burnet 5, Williamson 3, Tom Green 1). Infobox also lists 139+. Not a dam failure.
events.name: July 2025 Central Texas floods
events.geo_source: Kerrville / upper Guadalupe, a principal Hill Country flood zone in July 2025
events.what_happened: On 4 July 2025 a mesoscale convective vortex dumped extreme rain on the Texas Hill Country. The Guadalupe River at Hunt rose about 26 ft in 45 minutes. Wikipedia records 136 confirmed deaths (117 in Kerr County), with a few still missing. Camp Mystic on the Guadalupe was among the worst-hit sites. Governor Abbott and President Trump issued disaster declarations. Deadliest US inland flash flood since the 1976 Big Thompson flood.
events.cause_summary: Extreme summer rainfall over the Texas Hill Country, producing flash floods on the Guadalupe and neighbouring rivers.

events.name: 2026 Kenya floods
events.geo_source: Nairobi city centre (Wikipedia coordinates); Nairobi River burst its banks on 6–7 March
events.what_happened: Flash floods from the March–May 2026 long rains began on the night of 6–7 March when the Nairobi River burst its banks, killing 23 in the capital that night and disrupting flights at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. The National Police Service updated the nationwide death toll to 112 on 3 April 2026. About 6,953 households were affected and at least 34,765 people displaced by the end of March. The Kenya Meteorological Department had issued a heavy-rain warning on 25 February.
events.affected_or_evacuated: 6,953 households affected; at least 34,765 displaced by end of March (Wikipedia / Daily Nation)
events.cause_summary: Long-rains extreme rainfall over Nairobi and 30 counties; urban drainage and riparian settlement cited as aggravating factors.
events.notes: 112 is the National Police Service figure as of 3 April 2026, cited by The Star and the Wikipedia infobox. Later landslide deaths (18 on 3 May) are additional and not added into the 112 pin.

events.name: 2026 Assam floods
events.geo_source: Sivasagar city (Wikipedia coordinates); worst-hit district with 48 fatalities cited
events.what_happened: A 19 July 2026 cloudburst in Mon district, Nagaland, raised south-bank Brahmaputra tributaries and flooded Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat. The Hindu reported 98 deaths and more than 155,000 still affected as of 8 August 2026; the Wikipedia infobox lists 100+ deaths and more than 700,000 displaced. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma ordered door-to-door digital damage assessments. Ongoing as of mid-August 2026.
events.affected_or_evacuated: More than 700,000 displaced (Wikipedia infobox); 155,000 still affected on 8 August (The Hindu)
events.cause_summary: Cloudburst over the Naga hills; rapid rise of Brahmaputra south-bank tributaries. Some sources also cite deforestation and mining.
events.notes: Deaths left null because tallies are still moving: 85 (4 Aug), 98 (8 Aug, The Hindu / India Today, cited on Wikipedia), infobox 100+. Era 2026 because the event year is 2026.
events.inundation_area: About 10,748 ha cropland submerged (8 Aug sitrep cited on Wikipedia)
